STEP 1 - Scene: A tray meal (likely a cafeteria or catered lunch) photographed from a slightly elevated front angle, with several plates and bowls spread across the tray. The scale marker card with "3135" is on the table and is not food.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The main plate holding the sandwich is a disposable white plate about 22 cm in diameter (area ≈ 380 cm²). The salad plate on the right is oval, roughly 22 cm long, so I use a similar scale. The sushi plate is about 22 cm across. The vessel for the main analysis is the sandwich plate, ~380 cm². Other plates are at the edges and I size them against the same ~22 cm reference.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Sandwich/bagel-style roll with chicken salad filling (on the center plate)
- Sushi maki rolls, about 6-7 small pieces (left plate)
- Fresh spring/summer rolls or egg rolls, about 2 pieces (top center plate)
- Shredded cabbage and carrot salad with sliced chicken and herbs (right plate)
- Fruit cup: watermelon, cantaloupe, grapes, blueberries (small bowl, top right)
- Soy sauce in a small cup (no kcal counted in detail)

STEP 4 - Area (per plate, percent of its own vessel):
- Sandwich: ~60% of the 380 cm² plate, about 230 cm², piled ~5 cm tall including bread
- Sushi: ~35% of a 380 cm² plate, about 130 cm², ~2.5 cm tall
- Spring rolls: ~25% of a ~250 cm² small plate, about 60 cm², ~3 cm tall
- Chicken salad: ~70% of an oval ~330 cm² plate, about 230 cm², ~3 cm tall
- Fruit: ~60% of a small bowl ~200 cm², about 120 cm², ~3 cm tall

STEP 5 - Volume and STEP 6 - Grams:
- Sandwich: 230 cm² × 5 cm ≈ 1150 ml × 0.5 (roll with airy bread and filling) ≈ 575 g... bread-like items are lighter, so I take ~300 g for the whole sandwich.
- Sushi: 130 × 2.5 ≈ 325 ml × 0.7 ≈ 230 g... the pieces are small, so I take ~150 g.
- Spring rolls: 60 × 3 ≈ 180 ml × 0.6 ≈ 110 g.
- Chicken salad (cabbage, carrot, chicken): 230 × 3 ≈ 690 ml × 0.3 ≈ 200 g.
- Fruit: 120 × 3 ≈ 360 ml × 0.6 ≈ 215 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Sandwich (chicken salad on roll): 300 g × 230 kcal/100g = 690 kcal
- Sushi rice rolls: 150 g × 150 kcal/100g = 225 kcal
- Fried/fresh spring rolls: 110 g × 190 kcal/100g = 209 kcal
- Chicken and cabbage salad: 200 g × 120 kcal/100g = 240 kcal
- Fruit: 215 g × 50 kcal/100g = 108 kcal

Total ≈ 1,470 g and about 1,470 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Three full plates plus a fruit bowl with a large sandwich is plausible for a substantial lunch. The total of roughly 1.4 kg and about 1,500 kcal fits what is visible, though the sandwich weight is the most uncertain item.
